Subject: Request: Temporary retention carveout for Galaxy Therapeutics tenant

Hi Vanessa —

We have a regulatory investigation that requires Galaxy Therapeutics to retain a small set of inference debug traces and session logs for 120 days (our default Redwood TTL is 30d). The scope is limited to one tenant and a handful of trace IDs; legal needs proof-of-delete and a tamper-evident delivery of retained artifacts after the hold is lifted.

Could Redwood support a temporary retention exception for this tenant and share the artifacts you can provide as SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ evidence (manifest of deleted items, deletion timestamps, hash proofs, and who performed the deletion)? If there are limits (e.g., on private deployments vs hosted), please call them out.

Also: can you confirm if logs are stored with customer-scoped encryption keys and whether we can request an export prior to deletion? We want a short list of required documents so our legal and compliance teams can close the loop.

Thanks,
Emily Cole
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Galaxy Therapeutics

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the heads-up and the legal notice. We can support scoped temporary retention in the hosted environment but there are a few implementation details to confirm before we proceed:

- Scope: exact tenant ID(s), sample trace IDs, and a matching time window. Please list the tenant UUID and up to 250 trace IDs (we can handle more but it affects delivery timeline).
- Duration: you requested 120d — we can do that as a one-time exception; recommend adding a hard cutoff and automatic enforcement.
- Evidence artifacts we can provide: deletion manifest (CSV with object keys + deletion timestamps), SHA256 hash proofs for deleted objects, audit log extract showing the delete operation and operator identity, and a signed attestation from Redwood that deletion was completed as-of X date.
- Encryption/keys: for hosted tenants we use tenant-scoped encryption keys managed by Redwood KMS; we can perform an export for you before deletion but we cannot hand over master KMS keys. If you require key-handover we should discuss Private deployment options.

Next steps: I attached a short "retention exception request form" and an "evidence checklist" to help legal specify exactly what they need. Can you fill and return by EOD Monday? If so, Ben and Mina will scope the effort and I will propose an MAT (mutual action timeline) and a DocuSign for the attestation.

If helpful, I can schedule a 30-minute call with our security engineering lead (Mina) and Ben (customer ops) — proposed times: Fri 1pm PT or Mon 10am PT.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

My notes / proposed approach:
- We can implement a tenant-scoped hold by creating a retention policy in the serving runtime that marks the referenced KV keys and storage objects as exempt from normal TTL-based purge. This toggles a "hold" flag for the object's lifecycle controller.
- Deliverables: CSV manifest, audit log extract (w/ operator principal), and per-object SHA256. For additional assurance we can provide a signed attestation PDF generated by our legal team (DocuSign).
- Risk/ops: Holds increase storage exposure and affect efficient compaction. Recommend we limit to exactly the trace IDs provided and set an immutable expiration date.
- SOC2 implications: we should confirm with Kimberly whether providing pre-delete exported artifacts to the customer is acceptable under our SOC2 policy for hosted tenants; the CAIQ/SIG answers will need to reflect that exports are generated by Redwood and not by giving KMS access.

Action items for us:
1) Kimberly: confirm whether SOC2 control language allows the export/attestation flow as described and any additional artifacts auditors will expect.
2) Mina: estimate engineering hours to implement scoped hold + manifest generation + signed attestation (include QA).
3) Vanessa: get filled form from the customer and coordinate MAT + DocuSign.

Ben
